# Abstract

*Fragment.* Hydrological drought and low-flow forecasting at sub-seasonal to
seasonal leads is a memory problem: fresh indices decay while catchment
storage persists. We evaluate a recession-calibrated storage-deficit state —
fitted per catchment from its own training-year recessions (baseflow index,
recession constant, storage-outflow inversion for the storage scale) and
propagated by a mass-balance-verified fluid water balance — as a forecasting
feature across the CAMELS-IND large sample. The confirmatory question,
pre-registered before any test-year scoring, is whether the storage state
added to lagged standard indices beats the best of persistence, lagged
indices and an antecedent precipitation index at 3- and 6-month leads,
measured as paired per-gauge Brier differences on identical held-out months
(2011–2020) with a two-level block bootstrap. `[result sentence filled from
output/p1_confirmatory.csv once H1/H2 are scored.]` All state estimation is
verified by an exact three-way agreement (analytic recession solution,
fluid propagator, per-day ledger to 1e-9) and a 21-check battery; all
thresholds, screens, standardisation and tuning use training years only.

# Why the queue study retired

*Fragment.* The predecessor design read drought as a deficit queue. Its
confirmatory result (+0.002 Brier over SSI-3, 1–3 % relative; India arm
unresolvable at n = 12 of 472) was diagnosed as a design artefact: the queue
carried no information its benchmark lacked; the M/M/1/K class imported
artefact parameters (reneging, a service boost, blocking) with no
hydrological referent; and the utilisation screen selected catchments where
five assumed constants self-agree. The corrected re-run (Gate G2), with
dataset PET, a measured irrigated fraction, training-only thresholds and
honest memory baselines, is recorded in `STUDY.Rmd`; the queue is retired
from the forecasting path and retained only for climate-projection
reliability (Study P3), where its quantities are the product rather than a
benchmark contest.

# The storage state

*Fragment.* The state is millimetres of catchment storage:
$S(t+1) = \mathrm{clip}(S + P_e - E_a - Q_g, 0, S_{cap})$ with effective
input $P_e = \max(P - \varphi_m P, 0)$, supply-limited actual
evaporation $E_a = \min(\mathrm{PET}\,K_{c,m}, S + P_e)$ and a recession
release $Q_g = \min((K_a S)^{b_s}, S)$. $k$, $p$ (hence $b_s = 1/(2-p)$ and
$K_a = a/b_s$) and $S_{cap}$ come from censored recession segments of the
training record (Brutsaert-type inversion; 95th percentile of implied
storage); gauges with fewer than 20 segments borrow basin medians and are
flagged. Zero-flow days are censored: the state sits at its floor through a
zero-flow spell. Observed discharge never enters as a daily input — Q enters
only through the fitted recession law, which is what keeps the state's
memory different from a smoothed flow.

# Confirmatory design

*Fragment.* Two confirmatory contrasts (H1: 3-month lead; H2: 6-month lead),
each `storage_plus_indices` vs the per-gauge best-of
{persistence, lagged indices, API} frozen on training-year CV; H0 at
1-month lead is declared in advance as the parity/null expectation. Screens
are completeness and event-count only. Headline metric: Brier skill score
vs climatology; paired per-gauge deltas on identical held-out months;
two-level block bootstrap; sign test at >= 60 percent consistency; a declared harm
bound lists degraded gauges individually. **Announced limitation:** the
storage state is a different transform of the same record, not independent
information.

# Results

```{r results-confirmatory, eval=!is.null(conf), fig.height=4.2}
knitr::kable(conf[, .(hypothesis, lead, n,
  median_delta = sprintf("%+.4f", median_delta),
  CI = sprintf("[%+.4f, %+.4f]", boot_lo, boot_hi),
  sign = sprintf("%d/%d", sign_k, sign_n), verdict)],
  caption = "Confirmatory contrasts (India). Source: output/p1_confirmatory.csv.")
```

```{r results-bss, eval=!is.null(bss), fig.height=4.2}
med <- bss[is.finite(bss), .(bss_med = stats::median(bss)),
           by = .(family, lead, target)]
tw <- dcast(med, family + target ~ lead, value.var = "bss_med")
knitr::kable(tw, digits = 4,
  caption = "Median Brier skill score vs climatology by family and lead (India). Source: output/p1_bss.csv.")
```

# What remains open

*Fragment.* Lead-time skill structure by basin and climate class; zero-flow
and PET-source sensitivities; the US transfer arm as a descriptive check;
Study P3 (CAMELS-IND-Proj) as the follow-up where the frozen queue engine
publishes transient backlog probabilities and recovery times that no
standard index produces.
